blocks.text: Many pressure groups succeed by strategically combining ==PILs, media advocacy and public mobilisation==.

items.title: Positive
bullets: ==Democratises policymaking beyond the electoral cycle== — influence between elections, not just at the ballot box
Brings ==specialised/technical knowledge== into generalist bureaucratic decision-making
Landmark outcomes: ==RTI Act (2005), Forest Rights Act (2006), repeal of the farm laws (2021)==
Strengthens civil society's ==watchdog function== over state AND market

items.title: Negative / Structural
bullets: ==Elite capture== — business groups shape economic policy disproportionately vs labour or informal sector
==Opacity in lobbying== — India has ==no dedicated lobbying disclosure law==, unlike many OECD democracies
==Politicisation and co-option== — AITUC–CPI, INTUC–Congress, diluting independence
==Resource asymmetry== — grassroots and informal groups chronically underfunded
==FCRA tightening== has reduced NGO numbers and disrupted projects — a transparency vs civil-society-space tension
==Unconstitutional means== — bandhs, blockades and violence undermine legitimacy

items: ==Challenges==: factionalism within sectors (competing farmer unions); ==financial instability== of grassroots groups; ==party co-option==; no lobbying transparency law; FCRA-driven constraints; ==caste/communal polarisation==; urban-centric bias; no institutional permanence for anomic groups once the issue fades.

blocks.text: ==Key comparative lesson==: mature democracies (US, UK, EU) have moved to ==statutory lobbying registers and disclosure requirements==, converting an opaque practice into a transparent, regulated one. India has ==no equivalent central lobbying law== — pressure-group activity is governed only indirectly through registration and funding statutes.

items: ==Enact a lobbying transparency law== — on the lines of the ==US Lobbying Disclosure Act== or the ==EU Transparency Register==
==Institutionalise consultation== — mandatory public comment periods and ==Regulatory Impact Assessments== before major policy changes
==Rationalise FCRA implementation== — transparency without blanket restriction of civil-society space
==Formalise informal/non-associational groups== where feasible — peaceful, accountable, traceable channels
==Strengthen internal democracy and depoliticise== trade unions and associational bodies
==MSME and informal-sector inclusion== in business-group consultations
==Leverage digital platforms== for transparent, traceable donations and stakeholder engagement
